results.summary_before: This project implements a two-player Pong game that outputs to a VGA monitor and accepts input from two NES controllers. The NES controllers connect via three wires each to the bidirectional pins, and the VGA signals are output on the dedicated output pins. External hardware needed includes two NES controllers, a VGA breakout board (such as the Tiny Tapeout VGA PMOD), and a VGA-compatible monitor. The design is notable for combining classic gaming with retro controllers and a standard video interface.

The design is notable for being a compact, purely analog implementation of a flash ADC.

results.summary_before: This project implements a combinational logic-based pipeline hazard resolution unit for a RISC-V processor. It detects control, data, and structural hazards and generates signals to freeze the program counter, flush the pipeline, and indicate hazard-free execution. The design is tested in simulation by applying hazard scenarios and observing state transitions. It is self-contained and requires only a clock and reset, with no external hardware needed.

results.summary_before: This is a 3-bit flash analog-to-digital converter that samples a 0 V to 1.8 V signal on analog pin 0 and presents the result on three digital outputs. Its threshold voltages are built into inverter stages, so no external reference voltage is needed. Testing consists of applying a known input voltage and reading the three output bits, optionally with a multimeter. The design is a compact analog block whose main notable feature is the reference-free inverter-based comparator scheme.

results.summary_before: This design is an 8-bit Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) unit with a specialized SPST adder for efficient addition. It multiplies two 8-bit inputs to produce a 16-bit product, which is accumulated in an internal register. The lower 8 bits are continuously output, while the upper 8 bits are available on a bidirectional bus that can be externally overridden. It is optimized for Tiny Tapeout's limited IO and minimal area, and can be tested with simulation testbenches or Cocotb.
